newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Deutsche Bank launches A$250 mln FRN.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank launches A$250 mln FRN.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Tuesday it had launched a A$250 million principal subordinated floating rate extendible note through lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Australia Ltd.
The issue has been rated AA-plus by Standard and Poor's and a rating from Moody's Investor Services has been requested, Deutsche said in a statement.
"The issue is fully underwritten and is expected to raise A$250 million with the provisions for oversubscriptions," Deustche said.
The issue is scheduled to be priced on May 27.
Only the principal component of the notes is subordinated, and the notes have a tenor of 10 years with the margin to be determined on the pricing date by investor demand.
The notes are non-callable by the issuer but are extendible at the investor's option to 15 and then 20 years with a step up margin to 30 basis points.

"Deutsche Bank AG recognised the efficient pricing and improving depth in the Australian market for well-rated non-government issues and supported the use of the local Australian market," Deutsche group treasurer Chum Darvell said.

It is the first subordinated debt issue in the Australian market by local branch of a foreign bank, and is the first large issue since the A$200 million issue by the State Bank of New South Wales in September 1990, the statement said.
